messages:
incident-bot: Paging: Streaming p99 latency above SLO for pool-prod-gpu-2 — p95=0.45s, p99=12.3s, streaming stalls=320 (last 10m). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/streams/pool-prod-gpu-2 :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: On it. Picking this up as priority P0. Which customers on pool-prod-gpu-2 right now?
alex: I see spikes correlated with high disk writeback on host host-gpu-22. dstat shows heavy nvme write. Could be noisy tenant doing large checkpoints.
priya: Confirming. Traces show long tail waiting on IO -> backend read timeouts and streaming stalls. Suspect cgroup blkio throttle or runaway model checkpointing jobs.
oncall-sre: Quick check: who owns host-gpu-22? infra-bot: host-gpu-22 assigned to pool-prod-gpu-2, tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-beta, tenant-gamma, tenant-delta.
alex: Running quick top-like check for GPU processes:```ssh ops@host-gpu-22 sudo nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv``` Output shows a single heavy process: pid 41234 (tenant-beta-worker), sustained GPU mem and high disk IO.
priya: Also pulled `iostat -x 1 5` and seeing avg await ~120ms, %util ~95% on nvme2.
oncall-sre: Impact: customer streaming p99 SLO (8s) breached for 9 minutes, affecting multiple customers on the pool. We need live mitigation: options: 1) throttle noisy tenant cgroup/io, 2) migrate tenant to spare pool, 3) bump routing to fallback models. Which is fastest?
alex: Easiest quick action: reduce tenant-beta IO weight and evict background checkpoint process. I can push a cgroup update.
priya: Agree. Also start migration in parallel if throttle fails.
product-ops: Heads-up — one large customer on tenant-beta (enterprise-42) might see degradations. Product wants a short customer note if mitigation will take >15m.
infra-bot: Running `sudo cgset -r blkio.weight=100 /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-beta` now...
incident-bot: Action logged: cgroup blkio weight update initiated by infra-bot at 5155552240.
alex: Also killed a runaway `checkpoint.sh` background process: `sudo pkill -f checkpoint.sh --signal SIGTERM` (pid 41267).
priya: After throttle + kill: streaming stalls dropped to 18 (last 5m), p99 down to 1.9s. Still above baseline but much better.
oncall-sre: Good. Start migration of tenant-beta to spare pool as a durable fix. infra-bot: Starting live migration job `migrate-tenant tenant-beta spare-pool-1` — estimated 6m.
infra-bot: Migration progress: 30% -> 60% -> 100% (complete) at 5155552268.
priya: KV cache warming note: after migration, we see cold-start latency for tenant-beta requests; but cross-tenant impact removed. Overall pool p99 stabilized to 0.6s, p95 0.42s, stalls 2 (last 5m).
customer-success: Drafting customer notification for enterprise-42: "We've mitigated an incident affecting streaming latency for your workloads on shared GPU pools. Root cause: noisy background checkpointing causing NVMe saturation; we moved your workload to a dedicated spare pool and applied IO limits. If you saw errors, please forward logs and we'll review." Need approval?
product-ops: Approve. Keep it simple, mention that there's no data loss and our engineers will follow up.
oncall-sre: Follow-ups / action items: 1) postmortem (owner: oncall-sre) 2) add auto-detection rule: if pool p99 > 3s and nvme %util > 85% -> auto-evacuate offending tenant (owner: eng-platform) 3) add a safeguard to prevent checkpoint jobs on shared pools (owner: eng-ml) 4) add tenant-level IO throttling defaults (owner: eng-infra).
alex: I'll attach logs and `strace` snippet for the killed process to the incident ticket.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 5155552275. Status: degraded->healthy.
oncall-sre: Closing timeline: root cause = tenant-beta background checkpointing saturating NVMe -> cgroup blkio limits insufficient for this pattern -> tail latency spikes and streaming stalls for pool. Remediation = emergency blkio throttling, kill checkpoint, migration to spare pool, create follow-up tasks.
product-ops: Customer impacted: enterprise-42 (tenant-beta). No SLA credit currently decided.
customer-success: Sent notification to enterprise-42 (copy of message).
priya: We should also consider adding streaming backpressure metrics per tenant to detect this sooner.
oncall-sre: Agree. I'll open the postmortem doc and link follow-up tasks. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
